The maintenance of the weather station is an important process, which should be conducted meticulously over the suggested period of time. This process includes the cleaning of certain parts of the outdoor unit and the replacement of batteries. The maintenance process is summarised in the following steps.
documents.s: Maintenance of WeatherXM H2 Open Edition (WS2001)

documents.t: Clean the rain gauge at least once every 3 months. Rotate the funnel counter-clockwise and lift to expose the rain gauge mechanism and clean with a damp cloth. Remove any dirt, debris and insects. If bug infestation is an issue, spray the array lightly with insecticide. It is important not to swing the rain gauge spoon during this process, as the weather station will measure and record faulty precipitation. The sketch below shows how to open the rain gauge.
Clean the solar panel at least every 3 months with a damp cloth.

Remove any dirt, debris and insects from the thermo-hygro sensor every 12 months. It may be needed to open the radiation shield using a screwdriver and fully clean the thermo-hygro sensor in case there is too much debris on it. note You should occasionally check the battery status of the weather station: the decoded uplink includes battery_low (see Payload format), and the web flasher shows the battery on the station card. If the battery is low, replace all batteries with new ones of the same type. In harsh environments, inspect the batteries every 3 months (e.g. when cleaning the solar panel).

Most issues fall into one of three groups: connecting to the station over Bluetooth, the station joining your LoRaWAN network, and decoding its data. Start with the section that matches what you see. Quick checks Stay within a few metres of the station while using the web flasher (Bluetooth range is about 10m/32ft with few obstacles). Watch the red LED at the bottom of the station: breathing (slowly fading) means it is joining a network, off means it has joined, short blinks mean a computer or phone is connected over Bluetooth. Disconnecting from the web flasher always restarts the station, which then joins again. This is normal.

Use Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge on a computer or an Android phone. Safari, Firefox and iPhone/iPad browsers do not support Web Bluetooth. Check that Bluetooth is switched on, and on Windows and macOS that the browser is allowed to use it. Restart the station with one short press of the reset button at the bottom. The LED flashes a few times when it restarts. Click Connect again and look for WeatherXM WS2001 XXXXXX (older units: WeatherXM WS2000 XXXXXX), where XXXXXX is the end of the DevEUI. If the station is connected to another computer or phone, it does not appear: only one Bluetooth connection at a time is possible.
documents.s: The browser cannot find the station

documents.t: A computer or phone that has never connected to this station can only pair during the first 5 minutes after the station starts. Restart the station (one short press of the reset button) and connect within 5 minutes. If the station was factory reset since your last connection, remove it from your computer's or phone's Bluetooth settings ("Forget" / "Remove device") and pair again. The first pairing on a computer can take up to half a minute: the flasher shows Waiting for Bluetooth pairing…. If your operating system shows a pairing prompt, accept it. If the connection hangs, click Cancel and disconnect (or reload the page), wait a few seconds and connect again.
documents.s: Pairing fails, or it connects and then nothing happens

documents.t: During a firmware update the station restarts into update mode and appears in the Bluetooth list as DfuWX plus six characters (for example DfuWX467063), or as DfuTarg, not as "WeatherXM WS2001 …". Select that name. The station stays in update mode for about 2 minutes and keeps its current firmware until the new one is installed. If the update is interrupted, click Try again in the flasher to resume. If the 2 minutes have passed, the station restarts with its current firmware: connect again and start the update again.
documents.s: I can't find the station during the firmware update

documents.t: The station refuses firmware older than what it has installed. Nothing was changed and you can keep using the station.
documents.s: The update says the station "already runs a newer firmware"

documents.t: If the LED keeps breathing, the station cannot complete the join: Gateway coverage: check that your gateway is online and hears the station. On The Things Network open the gateway's Live data; on ChirpStack the gateway's LoRaWAN frames. If the gateway shows nothing from the station, it is out of range: move the station, the gateway, or both, and keep obstacles (walls, roofs, metal) out of the way. Region: the region set in the flasher must match your gateway and the device's frequency plan on the network server (for example EU868 everywhere, or US915 with Sub-Band 2 everywhere). Keys: the DevEUI, JoinEUI and AppKey must be identical in the flasher and on the network server. A single wrong character in the AppKey makes the network server reject the join (TTN shows the rejection in the device's live data). LoRaWAN version: register the device as LoRaWAN 1.0.4 with RP002 1.0.3 regional parameters.
documents.s: The station does not join my network

documents.t: Install the WeatherXM decoder as the uplink payload formatter (TTN) or the codec of the device profile (ChirpStack). WeatherXM frames arrive on FPort 99. Decoders written for the SenseCAP S2120 do not understand them. Uplinks on FPort 3 mean the station still uses the legacy format set by older tools. Connect it with the web flasher and apply your settings again to switch to the WeatherXM frame. Uplinks on FPort 199 come from firmware older than V4.6, which kept sending background messages meant for the WeatherXM network. Connect with the web flasher to update the station; the decoder labels these messages modem_service.
documents.s: Uplinks arrive but are not decoded

documents.t: On The Things Network each device may use 30 seconds of airtime per day. Use an upload interval of 5 minutes or more, and 10 minutes or more when the station is far from the gateway. See TTN fair use.
documents.s: Uplinks are missing, or the network warns about airtime

documents.t: The station keeps its WeatherXM settings, so it can potentially return to the WeatherXM network. The Switch back to WeatherXM button in the web flasher activates them and restarts the station; a factory reset does the same. If the station does not rejoin the WeatherXM network, contact WeatherXM support with its DevEUI (shown in the web flasher).

A factory reset restores the factory settings, erases all paired (bonded) computers and phones, resets the rain counter and activates the station's WeatherXM network settings, so it stops using your network. Your own network settings stay stored; to use your network again, apply your settings with the web flasher. warning Remove the station from your computer's or phone's Bluetooth settings right before the factory reset, so you can pair again afterwards. After the reset the station restarts and accepts new pairings for 5 minutes. To perform the factory reset, hold down the middle button on the bottom of the weather station, count to ~10 and release. The LED flashes very quickly to confirm the reset, then the station restarts.
You can find our team in our Discord Community Server. Alternatively, you can always contact us through support for any questions or issues you may have.

This page shows how to register the H2 Open Edition on The Things Network (TTN) and ChirpStack, and how to decode its data with the WeatherXM payload decoder. Do this together with Connect to Your Network: you take the DevEUI from the web flasher, and give the flasher the JoinEUI and AppKey you registered here.
documents.s: The Things Network and ChirpStack with WeatherXM H2 Open Edition (WS2001)

documents.t: Setting Value Activation OTAA LoRaWAN version 1.0.4 (MAC V1.0.4) Regional Parameters RP002 Regional Parameters 1.0.3 Device class Class A DevEUI From the web flasher (16 hex characters, the last 6 are in the station's Bluetooth name) JoinEUI / AppEUI Your choice, for example 0000000000000000 on TTN AppKey Your choice: generate it on your network server, then enter it in the web flasher Uplink port FPort 99 (24-byte WeatherXM frame)

1. Register the device 2. Add the decoder 3. Check live data Faster: import file from the web flasher In the web flasher, fill in the network form (click Generate Random for the AppKey) and click Download TTN import file (.json). In your TTN application open End devices > Import end devices, choose The Things Stack JSON, select the file and click Import end devices. The file sets the DevEUI, JoinEUI, AppKey, LoRaWAN version and frequency plan, so you can skip the manual steps below. It contains your AppKey: keep it private. In the TTN Console, choose your cluster (for example Europe 1) and open or create an Application. Click Register end device and select Enter end device specifics manually. Frequency plan: the plan of your region, for example Europe 863-870 MHz (SF9 for RX2 - recommended) or United States 902-928 MHz, FSB 2 (used by TTN). LoRaWAN version: LoRaWAN Specification 1.0.4. Regional Parameters version: RP002 Regional Parameters 1.0.3. JoinEUI: enter 0000000000000000 (or your own) and click Confirm. DevEUI: paste the DevEUI shown in the web flasher. AppKey: click Generate, then copy the key (eye icon, then copy). You will enter it in the web flasher. End device ID: for example ws2001-8000e6. Click Register end device. Now enter the same JoinEUI and AppKey in the web flasher. Open the device (or the whole application) and go to Payload formatters > Uplink. Formatter type: Custom Javascript formatter. Paste the WeatherXM decoder (or use the TTN v3 copy button in the web flasher). To test it, paste this example into Byte payload, set FPort to 99 and click Test decoder: F0454E0519EB00710E181F3400393000000C0031D4009427 Click Save changes. Open the device's Live data tab. After the station restarts you should see: Accept join-request Forward uplink data message FPort 99 Payload { "temperature": 23.5, "wind_gust": 5.2, ... } The first uplink arrives within a few minutes of the join, then one every upload interval. TTN fair use The Things Network community edition allows 30 seconds of airtime per device per day. A 24-byte uplink takes about 82 ms at SF7, so a 3-minute interval (about 39 s/day) exceeds it. Use the default 5 minutes (about 24 s/day), and 10 minutes or more when the station is far from the gateway and uses a slower data rate (SF9 to SF12). Private ChirpStack servers have no such limit.

ChirpStack v4 ChirpStack v3 1. Device profile (once for all your H2 stations): Device profiles > Add device profile General: name WeatherXM H2 Open (WS2001), region of your gateway, MAC version LoRaWAN 1.0.4, Regional parameters revision RP002-1.0.3, ADR algorithm default. Join (OTAA / ABP): tick Device supports OTAA. Class-B / Class-C: leave both off (Class A). Codec: Payload codec JavaScript functions, then replace the template with the WeatherXM decoder (or the ChirpStack v4 copy button in the web flasher). The same decodeUplink function works in ChirpStack v4. 2. Device: Applications > your application > Add device Device EUI: the DevEUI from the web flasher. Join EUI: your JoinEUI (any 16 hex characters, for example 0000000000000000). Device profile: the profile above. Click Submit. On the OTAA keys tab enter or generate the Application key, then enter the same key in the web flasher. 3. Check: the device's Events tab shows the join and then up events; the decoded values appear under object. Device-profiles > Create: LoRaWAN MAC version 1.0.3 (closest available), Regional Parameters revision B, Device supports OTAA. Codec: Custom JavaScript codec functions, paste the WeatherXM decoder (or the ChirpStack v3 copy button in the web flasher). ChirpStack v3 uses the Decode(fPort, bytes, variables) function, which is included in the same script. Applications > your application > Devices > Create: Device EUI from the web flasher, the profile above, then on Keys (OTAA) set the Application key.

Uplinks on FPort 99. Values marked "invalid" are sent when a sensor reports an error, and decode to null. Bytes Field Encoding 0 Frame type 0xF0 weather, 0xF1 weather + 64-byte signature, 0xF2 boot, 0xF3 GNSS scan 1 Firmware version High nibble major, low nibble minor (0x45 = V4.5) 2 Hardware / TX power Bits 7-5: hardware minor + 1, bits 4-0: TX power 3 Interval / battery Bits 6-0: upload interval in minutes, bit 7: battery low 4 Samples Number of 12-second samples in the interval 5-6 Temperature int16 little-endian, 0.1 °C (0x7FFF invalid) 7-8 Humidity / wind direction uint16 big-endian: bits 15-9 %RH (0x7F invalid), bits 8-0 degrees (0x1FF invalid) 9-10 UV / wind speed uint16 big-endian: bits 15-11 UV index (0x1F invalid), bits 10-0 0.1 m/s average (0x7FF invalid) 11-12 Wind gust uint16 little-endian, 0.1 m/s, highest 12-second peak of the interval (0xFFFF invalid) 13-16 Rain total uint32 little-endian, 0.001 mm, lifetime counter (0x7FFFFFFF invalid) 17-18 Rain rate uint16 little-endian, 0.1 mm/h, maximum of the interval 19-21 Light uint24 little-endian, lux (0x7FFFFF invalid) 22-23 Pressure uint16 little-endian, 0.1 hPa (0xFFFF invalid) Signed frames (0xF1) carry the same 24 bytes followed by a 64-byte ECDSA P-256 signature from the station's secure element. They are sent once after start-up and then every 7,200 uplinks. They need 88 bytes, which is possible from EU868 DR3 (SF9) upwards; at slower data rates, or if the secure element cannot sign, the station sends the normal 24-byte frame instead (firmware V4.6 and later). Boot frames (0xF2) are sent once after start-up with the firmware version and the sensor protocol version. GNSS frames (0xF3) carry a raw LR1110 satellite scan; resolve them with a GNSS solver if you need the position. They are off by default on your own network (firmware V4.7 and later, see GNSS location). FPort 199 is used only on the WeatherXM network (time sync and device status for its backend). From firmware V4.6 the station sends nothing on FPort 199 on your own network; the decoder labels any such message as modem_service. Rain: compute rain over any period from the difference of two rain_accumulated values.

The example payload above decodes to: { "firmware_version": "4.5", "hardware_version": "1.1", "tx_power": 14, "frame": "weather", "upload_interval_min": 5, "battery_low": false, "samples": 25, "temperature": 23.5, "humidity": 56, "wind_direction": 270, "uv_index": 3, "wind_speed": 3.1, "wind_gust": 5.2, "rain_accumulated": 12.345, "rain_rate": 1.2, "lux": 54321, "pressure": 1013.2, "pressure_pa": 101320 }

One script works in The Things Stack v3, ChirpStack v4 (decodeUplink) and ChirpStack v3 (Decode). It decodes the WeatherXM frame on FPort 99, labels FPort 199 messages from older firmware as modem_service, and, for stations configured with older tools, reads the legacy format on FPort 3. The web flasher can show, copy and download the same script. WeatherXM H2 / WS2001 uplink decoder (JavaScript) // WeatherXM WS2001 / WS2000 uplink decoder (WeatherXM firmware V3.x - V4.5+) // // Paste this whole file as-is into: // - The Things Stack v3: Application > Payload formatters > Uplink > Custom JavaScript // - ChirpStack v4: Device profile > Codec > JavaScript functions // - ChirpStack v3: Device profile > Codec > Custom JavaScript (uses Decode() below) // // Frames on FPort 99 (WeatherXM format, AT+TESTMODE_TYPE=0, the default): // 0xF0 24-byte weather frame (1 Helium data credit) // 0xF1 same, followed by a 64-byte ECDSA P-256 signature from the station's secure element // 0xF2 12-byte boot frame (firmware/hardware version, sensor protocol version) // 0xF3 GNSS scan (raw LR1110 NAV message; resolve with a GNSS solver) // Frames on FPort 3 (legacy "Open LoRaWAN" TLV, AT+TESTMODE_TYPE=1) are decoded too. // FPort 199 carries LoRa Basics Modem service messages (time sync for GNSS, device // management); they hold no weather data and are returned as { frame: "modem_service" }. // // Source of truth: ws2001-firmware/tools/decoders/ws2001_uplink_decoder.js // (byte layout: application/smtc_board/bsp/peripherals/ccl_sensor/sensor_data.c) function wxmHex(bytes, start, end) { var s = ""; for (var i = start; i < end && i < bytes.length; i++) { s += (bytes[i] < 16 ? "0" : "") + bytes[i].toString(16); } return s; } function wxmU16le(b, i) { return b[i] | (b[i + 1] << 8); } function wxmU24le(b, i) { return b[i] | (b[i + 1] << 8) | (b[i + 2] << 16); } function wxmU32le(b, i) { return (b[i] | (b[i + 1] << 8) | (b[i + 2] << 16) | (b[i + 3] << 24)) >>> 0; } function wxmDecodeWeatherXM(bytes) { var data = {}; var tag = bytes[0]; if (bytes.length < 3) return { errors: ["frame too short"] }; data.firmware_version = (bytes[1] >> 4) + "." + (bytes[1] & 0x0f); var hw = (bytes[2] >> 5) & 0x07; data.hardware_version = hw > 0 ? "1." + (hw - 1) : "unknown"; data.tx_power = bytes[2] & 0x1f; if (tag === 0xf2) { data.frame = "boot"; if (bytes.length >= 12) { data.boot_nonce = wxmHex(bytes, 3, 11); data.sensor_protocol_version = bytes[11]; } return { data: data }; } if (tag === 0xf3) { return { data: { frame: "gnss_scan", gnss_status: bytes[1], gnss_length: bytes[2], gnss_raw: wxmHex(bytes, 3, bytes.length) } }; } if (tag !== 0xf0 && tag !== 0xf1) return { errors: ["unknown frame tag 0x" + wxmHex(bytes, 0, 1)] }; if (bytes.length < 24) return { errors: ["weather frame must be 24 bytes, got " + bytes.length] }; data.frame = tag === 0xf1 ? "weather_signed" : "weather"; data.upload_interval_min = bytes[3] & 0x7f; data.battery_low = (bytes[3] & 0x80) !== 0; data.samples = bytes[4]; var t = wxmU16le(bytes, 5); data.temperature = t === 0x7fff ? null : (t & 0x8000 ? t - 0x10000 : t) / 10; // °C var hd = (bytes[7] << 8) | bytes[8]; data.humidity = (hd >> 9) === 0x7f ? null : hd >> 9; // %RH data.wind_direction = (hd & 0x1ff) === 0x1ff ? null : hd & 0x1ff; // degrees var uw = (bytes[9] << 8) | bytes[10]; data.uv_index = (uw >> 11) === 0x1f ? null : uw >> 11; data.wind_speed = (uw & 0x7ff) === 0x7ff ? null : (uw & 0x7ff) / 10; // m/s, mean of 12 s averages var g = wxmU16le(bytes, 11); data.wind_gust = g === 0xffff ? null : g / 10; // m/s, max of 12 s peaks var r = wxmU32le(bytes, 13); data.rain_accumulated = r === 0x7fffffff ? null : r / 1000; // mm, lifetime counter data.rain_rate = wxmU16le(bytes, 17) / 10; // mm/h, max over the interval var lx = wxmU24le(bytes, 19); data.lux = lx === 0x7fffff ? null : lx; var p = wxmU16le(bytes, 22); data.pressure = p === 0xffff ? null : p / 10; // hPa data.pressure_pa = p === 0xffff ? null : p * 10; if (tag === 0xf1 && bytes.length >= 88) data.signature = wxmHex(bytes, 24, 88); return { data: data }; } function wxmDecodeLegacyTlv(bytes) { var data = {}; var i = 0; while (i < bytes.length) { var id = bytes[i++]; if (id === 0x01 && i + 10 <= bytes.length) { var rawTemp = (bytes[i] << 8) | bytes[i + 1]; if (rawTemp & 0x8000) rawTemp -= 0x10000; data.temperature = rawTemp / 10; data.humidity = bytes[i + 2]; data.lux = ((bytes[i + 3] << 24) >>> 0) + (bytes[i + 4] << 16) + (bytes[i + 5] << 8) + bytes[i + 6]; data.uv_index = bytes[i + 7] / 10; data.wind_speed = ((bytes[i + 8] << 8) | bytes[i + 9]) / 10; i += 10; } else if (id === 0x02 && i + 8 <= bytes.length) { data.wind_direction = (bytes[i] << 8) | bytes[i + 1]; var rawRain = ((bytes[i + 2] << 24) >>> 0) + (bytes[i + 3] << 16) + (bytes[i + 4] << 8) + bytes[i + 5]; data.rain_rate = rawRain / 1000; var rawPress = (bytes[i + 6] << 8) | bytes[i + 7]; data.pressure = rawPress / 10; data.pressure_pa = rawPress * 10; i += 8; } else if (id === 0x03 && i + 1 <= bytes.length) { data.battery = bytes[i++]; } else if (id === 0x04 && i + 9 <= bytes.length) { data.battery = bytes[i]; data.hardware_version = bytes[i + 1] + "." + bytes[i + 2]; data.firmware_version = bytes[i + 3] + "." + bytes[i + 4]; data.upload_interval_min = (bytes[i + 5] << 8) | bytes[i + 6]; data.gps_interval_min = (bytes[i + 7] << 8) | bytes[i + 8]; i += 9; } else if (id === 0x05 && i + 4 <= bytes.length) { data.upload_interval_min = (bytes[i] << 8) | bytes[i + 1]; data.gps_interval_min = (bytes[i + 2] << 8) | bytes[i + 3]; i += 4; } else if (id === 0x06 && i + 1 <= bytes.length) { data.sensor_error_code = bytes[i++]; } else { break; } } data.frame = "legacy_tlv"; return { data: data, warnings: ["Legacy Open LoRaWAN format (no wind gust / rain total). Set AT+TESTMODE_TYPE=0 for the WeatherXM frame."] }; } function wxmDecode(bytes, fPort) { if (fPort === 199) { return { data: { frame: "modem_service", raw: wxmHex(bytes || [], 0, bytes ? bytes.length : 0) } }; } if (!bytes || bytes.length === 0) return { data: {} }; if (fPort === 3) return wxmDecodeLegacyTlv(bytes); if (fPort === 99 || bytes[0] === 0xf0 || bytes[0] === 0xf1 || bytes[0] === 0xf2 || bytes[0] === 0xf3) { return wxmDecodeWeatherXM(bytes); } return { data: {}, warnings: ["Unexpected FPort " + fPort] }; } // The Things Stack v3 and ChirpStack v4 function decodeUplink(input) { return wxmDecode(input.bytes, input.fPort); } // ChirpStack v3 function Decode(fPort, bytes, variables) { var r = wxmDecode(bytes, fPort); return r.data || {}; }

Setting up the weather station is a process of several steps in order to make this system work properly and measure weather conditions as accurately as possible.

Screwdriver (not included) Metal wrench (not included) Batteries 1.5V not rechargeable (x6 AA) (not included) danger If you use rechargeable batteries, you may harm your device. caution In order to properly deploy the weather station, you will need six (x6) AA batteries. These are not included in the box. warning Using old and new batteries together, especially low-quality ones or used, increases fire risk. For safety, use high-quality batteries of the same age and type.

Step 1: Slide the battery box lock switch to unlock position. Push to open the battery box door according to the arrow direction. Step 2: Insert the 6 AA batteries according to the +/- polarity indicated. Step 3: Place and lock the battery box door. Step 4: Unscrew the battery door at the bottom of the weather station. Step 5: Insert the dummy battery to the battery compartment, make sure the +/- polarity is correct. Step 6: Replace the battery door which comes along with the external battery box, then tighten the battery door screw. warning Using old and new batteries together, especially low-quality ones or used, increases fire risk. For safety, use high-quality batteries of the same age and type. caution If the dummy battery is not installed in the correct orientation, no power will be provided and the LED indicator will not be flashing. danger Rechargeable batteries should not be used, as they provide lower voltages and lose power over time. Solar panel is not trying to charge the batteries, but only provides power to an internal super capacitor, thus no point using rechargeable ones. danger Batteries should not be installed backwards. This may permanently damage the weather station. Although alkaline batteries are sufficient for most climates, lithium non-rechargeable batteries could be used for cold weather climates. The primary power source for the weather station is the solar panel. When solar power is available (sun light) a super capacitor is charged and is later used during night and when there is insufficient solar light. In climates that frequently sustain temperatures below 0°C or 32°F the use of lithium batteries is recommended as these are performing better than alkaline batteries under such circumstances, but depend on battery manufacturer and quality. note In case that LED is permanently on or does not light up at all, make sure that the batteries are inserted fully and in the correct way.

At the bottom of the weather station there are buttons and indicators: Once the batteries are inserted, the LED indicator on the back of the station should turn on for 4 seconds and then flash every 16 seconds indicating that the station transmits the data.

The tilting angle of the solar panel can be adjusted vertically from 0° into 15°, 30°, 45° and 60° positions depending on the area you are living in. For optimal power output year-round, please set the tilt angle that is closest to your latitude. Set tilt angle of solar panel related to your location Location ( latitude, longitude) Solar panel tilt angle Hamburg (53.558, 9.7874) 60° Chicago (42.1146, -88.0464) 45° Houston (29.7711, -95.3552) 30° Bangkok (14.2752, 100.5684) 15° Sydney (-33.5738, 151.3053) * 0° *Sensors installed in southern hemisphere must have their solar panels flat to ensure maximum solar efficiency. danger If the screw holding the solar panel is not released for the adjustment, there is a risk of breaking the plastic enclosure. caution Do not remove solar panel protection film before assemble battery box properly. Step 1: Remove the solar panel protection film. Step 2: Loosen the screw lightly until the gears on the opposite side separated from lock position. Step 3: Adjust the vertical angle of the solar panel (0°, 15°, 30°, 45°, 60°) according to the latitude of your location. Step 4: Push the gear and tighten the screw until the gears are securely locked.
The weather station receives all meteorological data and presents it on the screen of your smartphone. In this chapter, you will find guidance to set up the WeatherXM Helium station.
The station must be fully assembled (parts and batteries) A working smartphone with connection to the internet The WeatherXM Application installed on your smartphone.
Τo check if the weather station is in operation, check the red LED at the bottom of the station, it should light up - continuously or briefly - as soon as you insert the batteries.
Download our WeatherXM apps from their respective app store. Once you have your WeatherXM app, login to your account (you have to create a new WeatherXM account).

Start the Claiming Process Once you've logged in to your WeatherXM app, you will see an empty device list (assuming this is your first station setup). At the bottom right corner, you will see a "+" button. Tap it to start the claiming process of your station. Once you've done this, you'll be able to view all data of this station. caution Your first rewards will appear after 24 hours of the station being online.

info if you experience connection issues while claiming a helium device, make sure you are near the station. Reset your weather station and select device to pair​ Push the reset button at the bottom of your WeatherXM device to enable bluetooth pairing. This will expire in 5 minutes. After that, you will need to push it again to restart the pairing process. After that, push the "Pair station via bluetooth" button as seen in the picture below.

Select the Location that you'll Install your Station​ Allow access to your location so that the WeatherXM app knows where you are planning to install your WeatherXM station. Doing so will make it easier to complete this step. Alternatively, you can find the location manually using the map. Once you've found the right location, tap on the checkbox to acknowledge the correctness of the installation location and then tap on "Confirm and Proceed" button. note We do not track you, nor do we collect any data about your location. caution Make sure you select the location that you will install your station as precisely as possible, as this will take part in the quality of the data you will share with the network and thus your overall WXM rewards.

For the weather station to operate properly, you need to set its frequency to match the Helium network frequency in your country. A list of the countries and their respective frequencies can be found here. Given the location of installation you defined in the previous step, we’ve selected the appropriate frequency for that location. Once you've found the right frequency, tap on the checkbox to acknowledge the correctness of the installation and then tap on "Set & Claim" button. That's it. You've now claimed your new WeatherXM station and you'll be able to see its data on your WeatherXM apps! All you need to do now, is to update your weather station to the latest firmware version. To do so, please follow the instructions in the chapter "Update Firmware". caution The frequency selected above is the correct one the country you’ve installed and will operate this station. info Usually, it takes up to 30 minutes for the station to appear on the explorer

Included in the box WeatherXM Helium weather station External battery box Metal zip ties info Initial quantities included a short plastic pole accessory that was intended to be used with a wooden log to increase the total pole height to 2m. It was discovered that this accessory was not being utilised effectively, so it was removed from subsequent batches.

You would also need: Batteries 1.5V not rechargeable (x6 AA) Metal mounting pole (recommended 40mm/1.57in pole diameter & at least 2m/6.56ft height) Tools and parts to secure the pole danger If you use rechargeable batteries, you may harm your device

The weather station is a set of sensors encased in a plastic shell that ensures the proper function of the device. The weather station is responsible for the collection of measurements of temperature, humidity, rain rate, wind speed, wind direction, atmospheric pressure and UV index. Components Rain gauge Balance indicator UV and light intensity sensor Wind vane Wind cups Antenna Solar panel Radiation shield, temp/humidity, barometric pressure sensor Drain holes Built-in battery box Red LED indicator Config button Mounting clamp Adjustable hinge of solar panel Tipping bucket Rain sensor note For further details about an advisable installation of the weather station, please see Installing the WeatherXM Helium station (WS2000) Weather Station.
You can find our team in our Discord Community Server. Alternatively, you can always contact us through support for any questions or issues you may have.

Pole of at least 2m/6.5ft (not included) Base or bolts to secure in place (not included) Location and spacing Best Practices for Proper Station Installation caution It is imperative that you properly install your weather station. This will create the necessary conditions for quality weather data collection, which are required for the purpose of the WeatherXM network and the resulting rewards. Faulty installation, will result in less to none WXM rewards.

It is very important that your weather station collects quality measurements. This turns the weather station into a powerful tool for yourself and WeatherXM. The values of the various meteorological parameters measured by a weather station can significantly differ depending on the obstacles and the material of the surfaces existing around the sensors. For this reason, there is a series of criteria that should be fulfilled: info Not sure of your installation point? Check deployment examples here.
documents.s: Best Practices for Proper Station Installation

documents.t: The pole’s height, on which the weather station will be mounted, should be at least 2m/6.5ft. This means that the weather station should be placed at least 2m/6.5ft above the ground and any other horizontal or almost horizontal surface (e.g., roof) above the station. The maximum acceptable pole height is 5m/16.5ft.

The pole should be adequately tightened in order to prevent any pole oscillations in cases of strong winds. This will prevent the rain gauge spoon from swinging and collecting faulty precipitation measurements.

The pole together with the weather station should be placed in an installation point, which: 1. Is away from heat sources 2. Does not get in shadowed areas 3. Adequate Distance note All of 1, 2 and 3 are important tips for measuring temperature and humidity as accurate as possible while 3. is important for avoiding faulty precipitation and wind measurements.

Install the weather station in an open location with no obstructions above and around the sensor for accurate rain and wind measurement. Locate the North (N) marker on top of the weather station and align the marker to point North upon final installation with a compass or GPS. Tighten the mounting bracket around a 30-40mm or 1.1-1.57in diameter pole (not included) using the two screws and nuts provided. Use the bubble level on the weather station to make sure the sensor is completely level for proper measurement of precipitation, wind direction, UV and light intensity.
You just got your station, or, you will soon! Let's see what are the necessary steps in order to properly assemble, install, claim and enable it to send data in order to receive $WXM reward tokens.
Make sure that everything is in order and you're all set to proceed with station assembly. View Contents
Assemble all parts and make sure all sensors work as expected. For this step, you will need 6 AA batteries that are not included in the box. View Station Assembly Instructions

Once you've finished with installation, you can connect your station to the Helium network and claim it as your own in WeatherXM network. To do this, you will need to download our WeatherXM app (Android and iOS). View Connect and Claim Instructions

This is one of the most important steps, as proper installation is key in order to collect valid weather data. For this step, you will need a pole that is at least 2m/6.5ft and a way to secure it in place (both not included in the box). Here you will also see the best practices on how to properly install the station according to WMO. View Station Installation Instructions

The maintenance of the weather station is an important process, which should be conducted meticulously over the suggested period of time. This process includes the cleaning of certain parts of the outdoor unit and the replacement of batteries. The maintenance process is summarised in the following steps.

Clean the rain gauge at least once every 3 months. Rotate the funnel counter-clockwise and lift to expose the rain gauge mechanism and clean with a damp cloth. Remove any dirt, debris and insects. If bug infestation is an issue, spray the array lightly with insecticide. It is important not to swing the rain gauge spoon during this process, as the weather station will measure and record faulty precipitation. The sketch below shows how to open the rain gauge.
Clean the solar panel at least every 3 months with a damp cloth.

Remove any dirt, debris and insects from the thermo-hygro sensor every 12 months. It may be needed to open the radiation shield using a screwdriver and fully clean the thermo-hygro sensor in case there is too much debris on it. note You should occasionally check the battery level of the weather station via the settings menu on the mobile app. If the battery level is low, you should replace the batteries. In harsh environments, inspect the batteries every 3 months (e.g. when cleaning the solar panel).

If the process hangs and does not proceed or if pairing fails, try a factory reset.

Restart your station. Pairing is only allowed in the first 5 minutes after the station is started. After 5 minutes the station refuses pairing. If the problem persists, do a factory reset and try again.

If your station reports "No location data" please make sure your station is installed properly as per the installation instructions. note Your station reports its location a few times per day depending on network and battery status and thus it might take some time until the location is confirmed by the WeatherXM platform.

You receive a "location not verified" error on your mobile app when the Proof of Location (PoL) mechanism flags your weather station because the location reported by its GPS receiver(s) is different than the location you declared during the setup and claiming of the station. This happens because either you moved the station from its initial installation site, or you declared a wrong location during the onboarding of the station on your mobile app. This incurs a "relocation penalty" (as mentioned in the whitepaper) meaning your station will be exempt from reward distribution until the weather station is moved back to the declared location or the location is updated by using the "relocate station" function on your mobile app. After the passing of 7 days from fixing your location, the relocation penalty will be lifted and your station will start generating rewards as usual.

Make sure the device has started. Press the reset button at the bottom of the weather station. The light at the bottom of the station will flash a few times indicating that the restart was successful. If it continues to go undetected, try scanning again from a closer distance. The operating bluetooth range of the station is around 10m/32ft with few obstacles.

During factory reset all settings are reverted to the factory state, this includes the frequency configuration as well as the erasing of all bonded mobile devices. The erasing of the bonding information from the station results in the station "forgetting" all the mobile devices that have paired to it, so they will not be able to connect to the station anymore as they still hold old bonding data that is now outdated. In order to be able to pair with the station again the station must be unpaired on the mobile device as well, by removing it from the Bluetooth paired devices menu. warning It is recommended to unpair the station from your mobile device's bluetooth menu, right before performing the factory reset. This ensures you’ll be able to successfully pair again after the reset, during which the station will reboot and remain in pairing mode for a few minutes. After factory reset is complete and the station is paired to the mobile device again, the frequency needs to be set to the proper frequency used in your region via the station settings menu on your app or your station will not be able to join the network. To perform the factory reset, hold down the middle button on the bottom of the weather station, count to ~10 and release. The LED will start flashing very quickly as an indication that the factory reset has succeeded and then the station will restart.

In order for your station to keep operating normally and receive WXM rewards, you must update the station. The process is done wirelessly via bluetooth and requires you to be at a distance of ~<10m/32ft from the station. This document describes the firmware update process using an Android smartphone, the process for iOS is similar. Push the reset button at the bottom of your WeatherXM device to enable bluetooth pairing.This will expire in 5 minutes. After that, you will need to push it again to restart the pairing process. note Your mobile phone must be paired to your weather station for the mobile app to be able to communicate with it. This procedure needs to take place only once. All further communications do not require any pairing as your weather station stays paired to your mobile phone as long as it was not factory reset or the pairing manually removed in your phone. caution Make sure you don't move away from your station as you might lose bluetooth connection.

It is very important that your weather station collects quality measurements. This turns the weather station into a powerful tool for yourself and WeatherXM. The values of the various meteorological parameters measured by a weather station can significantly differ depending on the obstacles and the material of the surfaces existing around the sensors. For this reason, there is a series of criteria that should be fulfilled: info Not sure of your installation point? Check deployment examples here.

documents.t: The pole’s height, on which the weather station will be mounted, should be at least 2m/6.5ft. This means that the weather station should be placed at least 2m/6.5ft above the ground and any other horizontal or almost horizontal surface (e.g., roof) above the station. The maximum acceptable pole height is 5m/16.5ft.

The maximum acceptable pole height is 5m/16.5ft.

The pole should be adequately tightened in order to prevent any pole oscillations in cases of strong winds. This will prevent the rain gauge spoon from swinging and collecting faulty precipitation measurements.

The pole together with the weather station should be placed in an installation point, which: 1. Is away from heat sources 2. Does not get in shadowed areas 3. Adequate Distance note All of 1, 2 and 3 are important tips for measuring temperature and humidity as accurate as possible while 3. is important for avoiding faulty precipitation and wind measurements.
Setting up the weather station is a process of several steps in order to make this system work properly and measure weather conditions as accurately as possible.

Screwdriver (included) Metal wrench (included) Batteries, x2 AA not rechargeable (not included) danger If you use rechargeable batteries, you may harm your device. caution In order to properly deploy the weather station, you will need two (2) AA batteries. These are not included in the box.

caution Be sure that you place the wind cup assembly on the shaft at the top part of the sensor. The wind vane should be placed on the shaft at the bottom of the sensor. The wind sensor consists of a part that measures the wind speed (through wind speed cup assembly) and another that measures the wind direction (though wind vane). Both wind speed cup assembly and wind vane should be pushed onto the shafts on the part of the outdoor sensor, which is on the opposite side of the rain collector. Be sure that you place the wind cup assembly on the shaft at the top part of the sensor. The wind vane should be placed on the shaft at the bottom of the sensor. After pushing each of the parts, tighten the set screw with a Phillips screwdriver (size PH0). note Both parts should rotate freely. There should be no noticeable friction when the wind cup assembly rotates. However, the wind vane’s movement has a small amount of friction, which assists in providing steady wind direction measurements.

Use a screwdriver to open the battery compartment and insert 2 AA batteries. Once the batteries are inserted, the LED indicator on the back of the sensor should turn on for 4 seconds and then flash every 20 seconds indicating that the sensor transmits the data. Note that the LED flashing only indicates the transmission of the data from the outdoor sensor and it does not assure the reception of the data by the WG1000 gateway. Although alkaline batteries are sufficient for most climates, lithium non-rechargeable batteries could be used for cold weather climates. The primary power source for the outdoor sensor is the solar panel. When solar power is available, a super capacitor is charged and is later used during night and when there is insufficient solar light. In climates that frequently sustain temperatures below 0°C (or 32°F) the use of lithium batteries is recommended as these are performing better than alkaline batteries under such circumstances, but depend on battery manufacturer and quality. danger Rechargeable batteries should not be used, as they provide lower voltages and lose power over time. Solar panel is not used for charging the batteries, but only provides power to an internal super capacitor, thus no point in using rechargeable ones. danger Batteries should not be installed backwards. This may permanently damage the outdoor sensor.

Remove the black sticker from the solar panel. If not, batteries will deplete and then the station will switch off. note In case that LED is permanently on or does not light up at all,make sure that the batteries are inserted fully and in the correct way.

U-bracket installation​ The U-bolts and the metal plate are used to support the mounting of the outdoor sensor on a pole. The straight edge of the metal plate is inserted in the groove at the bottom of the unit (at the opposite side of the solar panel). The curved part of the 90-degree angle bent edge of the metal plate should be oriented to the wind sensor in order to “hug” the mounting pole. After inserting the metal plate, the U-bolts should be inserted through the respective holes of the metal plate. Loosely screw the nuts on the ends of the U-bolts. They will be tightened later when mounting on the pole (see Mounting the outdoor sensor).

The station must be fully assembled (parts and batteries). A working smartphone with connection to the internet. The WeatherXM Application installed on your smartphone. A reliable 2.4 GHz WiFi network (5 GHz is not supported) for the WG1000 Gateway to connect to.

The outdoor sensor is a set of sensors encased in a plastic shell that ensures the proper function of the weather station. The outdoor sensor is responsible for: the collection of measurements of local temperature, humidity, rain, wind speed and wind direction, and the wireless transmission of the data to the weather miner. Components Wind Speed Sensor Wind Vane Thermo-hygro sensor Rain collector Bubble level Solar panel Antenna Light sensor U-Bolts Battery compartment Reset button LED Indicator: light on for 4s on powers up. Then the LED will flash once every 16 seconds (the sensor transmission update period). This part of your weather station is placed outdoors. For further details about an advisable installation of the outdoor sensor, please see Installing the WS1000 Weather Station. The above figures show a sketch of the outdoor sensor. The sketch comes with a description of all the important parts and sensors of it.

The WG1000 Gateway is the device responsible for receiving weather measurements from the outdoor sensor and transmitting them via WiFi to IPFS and the WeatherXM network. The WG1000 Gateway is advised to be placed indoors, in an environment of relatively constant temperature (ideally within a daily range of <4°C/7°F for proper functioning of the barometer), near a window (for better GPS signal). The WG1000 Gateway should be permanently connected to power and powered on in order to be able to receive, record and upload measurements to the Internet. The above graph shows the location of the buttons and the needed connections. Briefly, there is a power and a reset button, a port for the GPS antenna and a USB Type-C port for power supply.

If this is the first time that you set up this outdoor sensor, then you should make sure that all parts work properly before mounting the sensor on the pole outdoors. Now, you may tighten the bolts with a wrench.
